request_debug.prompt_preview:
You write per-candidate post-mortems for a slopmortem pipeline. Given a fresh pitch and one dead-startup canonical document, produce a single LLMSynthesis JSON object that explains why this dead startup is similar, where the new pitch could diverge, what killed the dead startup, and what the new founder should learn.

Rules:
- Ground every claim in the candidate document or in tool calls. Do not invent facts.
- A `Trusted facts` block (typed pipeline data — not user input) appears below the pitc

response.text: {"candidate_id":"yo::social_communication","name":"yo","one_liner":"Single-function social notification app that sent only the word 'Yo' to friends; viral in 2014 but shut down by 2016 after hype faded and monetization never materialized.","similarity":{"business_model":{"score":4,"rationale":"The new pitch is explicitly ad-supported B2C, whereas Yo's trusted facts list monetization as tiered_freemium with a free price point. The document shows no evidence Yo ever ran ads or generated meaningful revenue. Both are free consumer mobile apps, but the revenue model is structurally different."},"market":{"score":6,"rationale":"Both target consumer mobile social communication, and both rely on a constrained, gimmick-style interaction (one-tap Yo vs. 30-second voice note from a single location). Both targeted young, viral-prone audiences. The sub-sector overlap (mobile messaging / social) is direct, though the new pitch anchors on a physical location mechanic absent in Yo."},"gtm":{"score":7,"rationale":"Both rely on organic viral growth within tight social clusters — Yo spread virally through Product Hunt and college-age users; the new pitch explicitly targets college towers as a viral wedge. Neither describes a paid acquisition strategy. The grassroots, hype-driven launch playbook is nearly identical."},"stage_scale":{"score":5,"rationale":"Yo reached global scale quickly (3M+ downloads, #1 social on App Store) after starting with a small employee group. The new pitch appears to be at an early/pre-launch stage targeting a campus niche, so stage alignment is partial — similar early viral strategy but the new pitch is earlier and more geographically constrained."}},"why_similar":"Both are minimalist B2C social mobile apps built around a single constrained communication gesture, targeting consumer audiences with a free product and a viral grassroots growth strategy. Yo's trajectory — explosive viral adoption in a specific community, rapid climb up app store charts, followed by inability to sustain engagement or monetize — mirrors the core risk profile of any novelty-driven, single-mechanic social app. Both share consumer customer type, global-capable product (iOS/Android), and a community-cluster go-to-market (Yo: Product Hunt + media hype; new pitch: college towers).","where_diverged":"Three concrete divergences: (1) Monetization model — the new pitch is ad-supported, whereas Yo was tiered_freemium with no documented ad revenue; this is a meaningful structural difference that gives the new pitch a clearer, if challenging, revenue path. (2) Content format — the new pitch centers on 30-second voice notes, a richer, more differentiated media type than Yo's single-word ping, which may support longer engagement loops. (3) Location anchor — the new pitch ties posts to a single recurring physical location (e.g., a dorm tower), creating a place-based community mechanic Yo never had; this could drive retention through local identity in a way Yo's purely social graph could not.","failure_causes":["hype-driven growth with no durable engagement loop","no viable monetization — tiered_freemium generated insufficient revenue","product too minimal to retain users once novelty wore off","security vulnerability (phone number leak) damaged early trust","feature creep to compensate for core weakness diluted the original value proposition","team abandoned active maintenance, company ran on 'autopilot' before shutdown"],"lessons_for_input":["Validate that your single-mechanic interaction drives repeat daily use before scaling — novelty alone has a short half-life, as Yo's decline after peak hype demonstrates.","Define your ad-supported revenue model with concrete CPM benchmarks and minimum MAU thresholds before launch; Yo never bridged from free to monetized and ran out of runway.","Harden security early — a single exploit (Yo's phone-number leak) can permanently damage trust in a social app where the entire value proposition is peer connection.","Use the location-anchor mechanic as your defensible moat and retention driver; resist the temptation to generalize the product to broaden reach, as Yo's feature additions failed to recover lost users.","Plan for post-hype plateau: map out what keeps users returning in month 6, not just month 1, and instrument retention metrics from day one."]}
